chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

A woman has no authority, alongside her husband, regarding emancipation, charity, tadbīr, gifting, or making a vow concerning her wealth except with her husband's permission, except in hajj, zakat, dutifulness to her parents, or maintaining ties with her relatives.

key_terms.تَدْبِيرٍ: declaring a slave to be freed after one's death
key_terms.نَذْرٍ: a vow concerning property or an act
key_terms.هِبَةٍ: a gift or endowment made voluntarily

ai.seo_question: What financial actions may a married woman undertake without her husband's permission according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a married woman's financial dispositions in certain matters while she is with her husband. It also identifies exceptions in acts of religious obligation and family righteousness, including hajj, zakat, dutifulness to parents, and maintaining kinship ties.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4514 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:

"A woman has no authority, alongside her husband, to emancipate (a slave), give charity, make a bequest, give a gift, or make a vow concerning her wealth without her husband's permission, except in matters of Hajj, Zakat, honoring her parents, or maintaining ties with her relatives."
